entries.title: Benjamini–Schramm criticality conjecture, original site form
entries.statement: Conjecture (not a theorem): Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph whose automorphism group has finitely many vertex orbits. In independent Bernoulli site percolation, if the critical parameter p_c(G) is below 1, then at p_c(G) there is almost surely no infinite open vertex cluster. This is the site-percolation form of Benjamini and Schramm's 1996 Conjecture 4; the p_c<1 assumption is essential.
assumptions: finitely many vertex orbits under Aut(G)

source.excerpt: Critical percolation dies in every almost transitive graph (assuming pc < 1).

entries.title: Benjamini–Schramm criticality conjecture, bond analogue
entries.statement: Conjectured bond analogue (do not treat as an established theorem without reviewing a current proof): Let G be an infinite connected locally finite graph with finitely many vertex orbits under its automorphism group. In independent Bernoulli bond percolation with p_c(G)<1, the configuration at p_c(G) almost surely has no infinite open edge cluster. Benjamini and Schramm expressly said their nonplanar questions extend to bond percolation; Hutchcroft's 2016 theorem proves the exponential-growth subcase. A September/October 2026 release claims the full bond statement, but that claim is not certified by this draft.
assumptions: finitely many vertex orbits under Aut(G)

source.excerpt: remain equally valid, with only minor modifications, for bond percolation

relations.rationale: The original paper frames Conjecture 4 in site percolation and explicitly extends its nonplanar questions to bond percolation. Both endpoint excerpts above are from that source; the relation does not assert that either conjecture is proved.
